text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLILTA

- Despite net losses accrued over the last few years the Gdynia shipyard (SG) will earn a net profit in 1997 thanks to the yard's restructuring, SG president Krzysztof Banaszak said. A group of banks will increase the company's capital by $100 million in three months time.
- Poland's consumer credits drawn last year increased by 6.1 billion zlotys, or 108 percent.

- More than 50 percent of the 350 employees of the Bydgoszcz-based IBIS baking equipment maker started a sit-in strike yesterday, the strikers' spokesman Wojciech Holz said. The strike was supported by Solidarirty and other trade unions.

- The Poznan-based Volkswagen (VW) plant will start assemblying the Polo model in the first quarter of 1997 and the Skoda Octavia model in the second quarter this year, VW Poznan director Adam Dobielinski said.

- The board of the Trzemeszno-based Izopol construction material maker has suspended till June a decision on dismissing 285 workers, who produced the recently banned asbestos and cement construction elements. The plant was allowed to carry out the asbestos elements' production for the next six months.
- A body of provincial governors has marked out 700 kilometres of motorways to be built in near future around the country, the Motorway Construction Agency (ABAE) president Andrzej Patalas said.

- Poland's coal mining losses reached over 1.586 billion zloty by the end of November 1996 . The cost of mining of one tonne of coal exceeded the market price by 6.57 zlotys but the total coal output grew by 0.8 percent last year, the Central Statistical Office ( GUS) said.

- Germany's Ludwig Schokolade GmbH confectionery maker will move praline chocolade production to Krakow, southern Poland. Ludwig has also set up a confectionery plant in Pila, northwestern Poland, which will produce 36 tonnes of chocolade pralines and six tonnes of chewing gum daily.
NOWA EUROPA
- Neither Poland nor Romania can afford to remain outside of the EU, Romania's President Emil Constantinescu said during his visit to Warsaw.

- The financial results of Poland's corporate sector in the first 11 months of last year were worse than in the same peiod in 1995 due to a significant cost growth, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.

- The listed Kompap paper maker will net 4.8 million zlotys on 56 million zloty in revenues this year, the company's forecast said. Kompap plans to invest seven million zlotys in development this year.
- A banking consortium headed by the listed AmerBank has provided a $7.6 million credit for a business complex construction in central Warsaw, AmerBank said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- The Economy Minister Wieslaw Kaczmarek is ready to allow the listed Universal foreign trade firm for a duty free imports of car parts for the assembly of Hyundai vehicles in Poland.
ZYCIE
- Canada's Propak Systems Limited will supply gas from the seams based in the Gorzow province to the Gorzow heat and power plant as of end-July 1998, according to a recently signed contract.

- The listed Optimus and JTT, Poland's leading computer makers, will soon introduce the Bravo MX 160 and MX 200 processors in their new hardware, which will cost up to 7,000 zlotys, the companies said.
PARKIET
- The Warsaw-based Bank Ochrony Srodowiska (BOS) environmental protection bank and the Kielce-based Poligrafia have applied to the Warsaw bourse board for a continuous share trading permit.
